title: Finite formal jet lengths are invariant under coefficient field extension
statement: Let $\iota:L\to E$ be an embedding of fields [def-weil-field], let $\sigma$ be a finite variable set, and let $K$ be any ideal of $L[[X_j:j\in\sigma]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $K_E$ for the ideal generated by coefficientwise images of members of $K$. For every $q\in\mathbf N$, the lengths [def-weil-pbc-module-length] of the respective ring modules satisfy $\operatorname{length}_{E[[X]]}(E[[X]]/(K_E+(X)^{q+1}))=\operatorname{length}_{L[[X]]}(L[[X]]/(K+(X)^{q+1}))$. Equivalently, the extendedHilbert functions of [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum] agree in each degree. No generator, division, characteristic-zero or proper-ideal assumption is imposed.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the route; BM 1997, Remark 3.8, p.234, (7.2), Lemmas 7.3 and 7.5, p.263, and proof of Theorem 9.4, p.278. Explicit scalar-extension argument written by V2 after reading the BM journal PDF in the sandbox scratchpad.

proof.text: The finitely many monomials of total degree at most q form a basis of the quotient of the formal series ring by (X)^(q+1): deleting higher coefficients gives representatives, and membership in that power means all these coefficients vanish. Choose a basis of the image of K in this finite monomial space, and lift it to finitely many elements of K.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the route; BM 1997, Remark 3.8, p.234, (7.2), Lemmas 7.3 and 7.5, p.263, and proof of Theorem 9.4, p.278. Explicit scalar-extension argument written by V2 after reading the BM journal PDF in the sandbox scratchpad.

proof.text: The image of K_E in the target monomial space is exactly the E-span of this chosen image basis. Indeed the ideal K_E consists of finite sums of target-series multiples of mapped source members. Modulo (X)^(q+1), truncate every multiplier to a polynomial. Each resulting source monomial multiple still belongs to K, so every product is in that E-span. Conversely each image basis vector lies in the extended ideal. Extend the source image basis to a basis of the entire truncated monomial space. Its invertible matrix and inverse remain inverse over E, proving equality of quotient dimensions.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the route; BM 1997, Remark 3.8, p.234, (7.2), Lemmas 7.3 and 7.5, p.263, and proof of Theorem 9.4, p.278. Explicit scalar-extension argument written by V2 after reading the BM journal PDF in the sandbox scratchpad.

proof.text: Filter either quotient by the images of powers of (X), from power zero through q+1. Each successive quotient is killed by (X). Its modules over the formal ring and over the coefficient field have the same submodule lattice, since the action factors through the surjective constant-coefficient map. Its length is therefore its finite vector-space dimension. Add lengths and dimensions along the finite filtration; both total lengths equal the respective quotient dimensions. Combine with the preceding dimension equality. A unit ideal gives zero modules; a zero-variable set leaves only the coefficient field, including q=0.
